## 6. Summary and self-check
One-paragraph essence, self-check items.
examShortTricks: Trick 1: Identify the fallacy bank: hasty generalisation, ad hominem, false cause, appeal to emotion — naming the flaw in an argument is the unit's core skill.
Trick 2: Evaluate claims with the CARS test: Claim, Assumptions, Reasons/evidence, Standard of proof — a quick scaffold for 'do you agree?' questions.
Trick 3: Distinguish fact (verifiable) from opinion (judgement) — quote one sentence of each from the passage to secure the marks.
practiceQuestions: Q. What is the difference between a fact and an opinion? (1 mark) — a fact can be verified; an opinion expresses belief or judgement.
Q. Identify one weakness in the writer's argument. (2 marks) — name the fallacy (e.g. hasty generalisation) and quote the offending line.
keyPoints: Critical thinking = questioning evidence, not rejecting everything — show balanced reasoning.
Structure: claim → evidence → evaluation → conclusion; examiners reward this order.
